items.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004
items.q: Everybody is happy, like they were really happy when they heard the records that I did on my own, the bluegrass records or the classical records, or the things with Edgar [Meyer].

ctx.x: Once in a while, although everybody is really good. They really understand because they all lead themselves. They all have their own groups and situations that they have to make those kinds of decisions about and I think that they are pretty cool with most things. Usually everything is about accommodation. That’s what the challenges are. Victor wants this time to do something. I’ve got a call to do this. Jeff might have this. Future Man might have this. But we have to work enough to keep this great crew that we…

everybody in the group could get to do cool stuff outside the group but me, who had all these great opportunities I was turning down all the time. But I never talked to them about it. It was just something that was going on in my own head and gradually I realized that I had to take care of myself too, that I had to be part of the equation of making everybody happy. It wasn’t just everybody else but me. It was me too. And that it turned out to not be an issue. Everybody is happy, like they were really happy when…
If someone brings a tune of their own to the group, they’re emotionally invested in it, but it’s just not a Flecktone song, is it really apparent to everybody?
